**Re: VAT Registration – Notification of Filing Requirements**

We write further to our previous correspondence regarding your VAT registration. This notice confirms the filing requirements that apply to your business for the current registration period.

**Quarterly accounting period**

Your VAT accounting period is the standard three-month period ending on the last day of March, June, September and December. For each accounting period, you must submit a VAT return to HMRC showing the amount of VAT you have charged on your sales and the amount of VAT you have paid on your purchases. The return must also show the net amount of VAT due to HMRC or, if you have paid more VAT than you have charged, the amount of VAT repayable to you.

**VAT Return Q1 2025**

The first return under your current registration covers the period 1 January 2025 to 31 March 2025. HMRC correspondence states that VAT Return Q1 2025 submission deadline is 2025-05-07. Record status: current. This date is current and applies to the return you must file for the January to March 2025 period. The return will cover all transactions you have recorded during this quarter, including any supplies you have made and any purchases you have received.

You should ensure that your records for this period are complete and accurate before you submit the return. If you identify any errors after submission, you may need to correct them on a subsequent return, depending on the value of the error and the time that has elapsed.

**Submitting your return**

You can submit your VAT return using HMRC’s online services or through MTD-compatible software. Once you have submitted your return, you will receive an acknowledgement from HMRC confirming that it has been received. You should retain this acknowledgement for your records.

If you cannot submit your return by the deadline, you should contact HMRC as soon as possible. In some circumstances, we may be able to agree a different date for submission, but you must request this before the deadline has passed. A request made after the deadline will not be treated as a valid application for an extension.

**Payment of VAT due**

Any VAT due for the quarter must be paid to HMRC by the same date as the return is due. Payment can be made by direct debit, bank transfer, or through your MTD-compatible software. If you pay by direct debit, you must ensure that your bank account has sufficient funds on the payment date. HMRC may charge interest on any VAT paid late, and you may also be liable to a surcharge if you do not pay on time.

If you are due a repayment, HMRC will normally make the payment within 10 working days of receiving your return, provided the return is accurate and complete. If you are due a repayment and you also owe VAT for a previous period, HMRC may offset the repayment against the amount you owe.

**Late submission of VAT returns**

Submitting VAT returns late is a serious matter. HMRC may charge a default surcharge if you do not submit a return by the due date. The surcharge is calculated as a percentage of the VAT that is unpaid at the date the surcharge is triggered. The percentage increases with each successive default within a 12-month period.

For the first default, the surcharge is 2% of the VAT outstanding. For a second default within the same period, the surcharge rises to 5%. For a third default, it rises to 10%, and for a fourth or subsequent default, it rises to 15%. In addition to the surcharge, you may also be liable to interest on any VAT that is paid late.
You are responsible for monitoring your taxable turnover on a rolling 12-month basis. This is not the same as your accounting year. You must look back at the total value of your taxable supplies made in the last 12 months at the end of every month. If, at the end of any month, the total for the previous 12 months has exceeded the threshold, you must register within 30 days.

The date of registration will be the date you became liable to register, which is the end of the month in which the threshold was exceeded. You will then be required to charge VAT on your supplies from that date, even if you have not yet received your VAT registration number.

**3. What Counts as Taxable Turnover**

For the purposes of the threshold, taxable turnover includes the total value of all supplies you make in the course or furtherance of your business that are subject to VAT at the standard, reduced, or zero rate. It also includes supplies that would be taxable if they were made in the United Kingdom.

The following are not included in your taxable turnover:

- Supplies that are exempt from VAT, such as certain financial services, education, and health services.
- Supplies made outside the UK that would not be taxable if made in the UK.
- Capital assets sold as part of a business transfer.
- Grants or subsidies that are not directly linked to the value of supplies.

If you make only exempt supplies, you will not normally be able to register for VAT. However, there are limited circumstances where you may be able to register voluntarily, for example, if you make certain types of exempt supplies to customers outside the UK.

**4. Voluntary Registration**

If your taxable turnover is below the threshold, you may still choose to register for VAT voluntarily. This can be beneficial if you make mostly zero-rated supplies and expect to reclaim VAT on your purchases, or if you wish to recover input tax on costs incurred before you become liable to register.

You should note that once you are registered voluntarily, you must remain registered for at least 12 months. If you wish to cancel your registration at the end of that period, you may do so provided your taxable turnover in the following 12 months is expected to be below the deregistration threshold.

HMRC correspondence states that VAT Threshold threshold amount is 90000 GBP. Record status: current.

**5. Deregistration Threshold**

The deregistration threshold is also reviewed annually. If you are registered for VAT and your taxable turnover in the next 12 months is expected to fall below the deregistration threshold, you may apply to cancel your registration. You should contact HMRC if you think you may be eligible to deregister.

**6. Effect of the Threshold on Group Registrations**

If you are part of a group of companies that is registered for VAT as a single entity, the threshold applies to the total taxable turnover of the group, not to each individual company. You should therefore monitor the combined turnover of all group members. If the group’s total taxable turnover exceeds the threshold, the group must register.

**7. Changes to the Threshold During the Year**

The threshold is set for the tax year beginning 1 April and ending 31 March the following year. Any changes to the threshold are announced in the Budget and take effect from the start of the next tax year. You should not assume that the threshold will remain the same from year to year.

**8. Penalties for Late Registration**

If you fail to register by the required date, HMRC may charge a penalty. The penalty is calculated as a percentage of the VAT that is due from the date you should have registered to the date you actually registered. The percentage is based on the reason for the failure, and whether it was deliberate or non-deliberate.

If you become aware that you should have registered earlier, you should contact HMRC as soon as possible. In some cases, we may reduce the penalty if you have a reasonable excuse for the late registration.

VAT return periods

HMRC VAT Registration Notice

Issued: 15 April 2025

Reference: VAT 405

This notice provides general guidance for businesses that have recently registered for VAT or are considering registration. It should be read alongside Notice 700, which contains more detailed information about how VAT works.

Record keeping

You must keep records of all business transactions that affect your VAT position. These records should be accurate, complete, and readable. You must keep them for at least six years, unless you have written permission from HMRC to destroy them earlier. Records may be kept on paper or in electronic form, provided they are readily accessible to HMRC when required.

Your records should include:

- your accounting records, including cash books, sales and purchase ledgers, and bank statements
- your VAT account, which summarises the VAT you have charged and the VAT you have paid
- copies of VAT invoices you have issued and VAT invoices you have received
- documentation relating to imports and exports
- any credit notes or debit notes you have issued or received
- records of goods and services you have supplied to yourself or to your staff for private use

Your VAT account must show, for each VAT return period, the total VAT due on your sales, the total VAT you can reclaim on your purchases, and the net amount payable to HMRC or reclaimable from HMRC. You should update your VAT account regularly and make sure it agrees with your accounting records.

Electronic records

If you keep your records electronically, you must ensure that the software you use can produce, in a legible format, all the information that HMRC may need to verify your VAT position. You must also ensure that the records cannot be altered without leaving an audit trail. You should take reasonable steps to protect your records from loss or corruption, including keeping backup copies.

Digital record keeping is a mandatory requirement for most businesses under the Making Tax Digital for VAT rules. If you are required to keep digital records, you must use functional compatible software to maintain your VAT account and file your returns. Further information is available in Notice 700/22.

Invoicing

You must issue a VAT invoice whenever you make a taxable supply to another business. You do not have to issue a VAT invoice for sales to private individuals, but you must be able to account for the VAT on those sales. You may issue a less detailed invoice for retail sales where the total amount including VAT is £250 or less. A less detailed invoice must show your name and address, your VAT registration number, the date of issue, a description of the goods or services, and the total amount payable including VAT.

If you issue a VAT invoice, you must keep a copy. You must not issue a VAT invoice for a supply that is exempt from VAT or that is outside the scope of VAT, unless the invoice clearly states that no VAT is chargeable.

Credit notes

If you allow a customer a reduction in the price after you have issued a VAT invoice, you must issue a credit note. The credit note must show the same information as the original invoice, together with the amount of the reduction and the VAT adjustment. You must keep a copy of every credit note you issue and you should ensure that your accounting records reflect the adjustment.

Filing your returns

You must submit a VAT return for each return period, even if you have no VAT to pay or reclaim. The return must be submitted electronically using compatible software. You should allow sufficient time to prepare your return and to submit it before the deadline. HMRC will not accept returns submitted by post unless you have received specific permission to do so.

Please quote your VAT registration number in all correspondence with HMRC and when contacting the VAT helpline. You should also retain this notice for your records as it confirms your registration status and effective date.

**What you need to do now**

Your first VAT return will cover the period from 1 February 2025 to 31 March 2025 and must be submitted to HMRC by 7 May 2025. You will need to account for VAT on all taxable supplies you make from your effective date of registration, including any services supplied from your office at the above address.

You may also be able to reclaim VAT on eligible business purchases made before your effective date, provided those purchases relate to your business activities and were made within the six months prior to registration (or four years for certain services). Any pre-registration input tax must be claimed on your first VAT return and supported by valid VAT invoices.

**General information about VAT registration**

When you are registered for VAT, you are required to keep accurate business records and maintain a clear audit trail of all transactions. This includes records of sales and purchases, VAT invoices issued and received, and any adjustments such as credit notes or bad debt relief. You must also retain copies of all VAT returns and any correspondence with HMRC for at least six years. Failure to keep adequate records can result in penalties.

You will need to file VAT returns electronically using HMRC’s online services or compatible software. Returns are due one calendar month and seven days after the end of each accounting period. Payment of any VAT due must be received by HMRC no later than the same date. If you expect to owe more than £23,000 in VAT each year, you will be required to make payments on account.

HMRC registration records confirm that LedgerWise Bookkeeping Ltd is registered for VAT with registration number GB123456789. Record status: current.

Most businesses are required to submit their VAT returns using Making Tax Digital (MTD) compatible software. This means you must keep digital records of your business transactions and file your returns using software that connects to HMRC’s systems. Spreadsheets are acceptable provided they are linked to bridging software that meets the MTD requirements.

**Your obligations as a VAT-registered business**

As a VAT-registered business, you must:

- Charge VAT at the correct rate on all taxable supplies you make.
- Issue valid VAT invoices to your customers, showing your VAT registration number.
- Keep a VAT account that summarises the VAT you have charged and the VAT you have paid.
- Submit VAT returns on time and pay any VAT due.
- Notify HMRC of any changes to your business details, including changes to your address, legal entity, or the nature of your activities.

If you are unsure about any of your obligations, you can refer to HMRC’s VAT guide (Notice 700) or contact the VAT helpline. The helpline is available Monday to Friday, 8am to 6pm, excluding bank holidays.

**Making Tax Digital for VAT**

From your effective date of registration, you must comply with the Making Tax Digital rules. You are required to keep digital records of your business transactions and submit your VAT returns using MTD-compatible software. If you currently use a manual bookkeeping system, you will need to move to a digital system before your first return is due. HMRC provides a list of compatible software on its website.

We write further to our previous correspondence regarding your VAT registration. This notice confirms the filing requirements that apply to your business for the current registration period.

**Quarterly accounting period**

Your VAT accounting period is the standard three-month period ending on the last day of March, June, September and December. For each accounting period, you must submit a VAT return to HMRC showing the amount of VAT you have charged on your sales and the amount of VAT you have paid on your purchases. The return must also show the net amount of VAT due to HMRC or, if you have paid more VAT than you have charged, the amount of VAT repayable to you.

The return will cover all transactions you have recorded during this quarter, including any supplies you have made and any purchases you have received.

You should ensure that your records for this period are complete and accurate before you submit the return. If you identify any errors after submission, you may need to correct them on a subsequent return, depending on the value of the error and the time that has elapsed.

**Submitting your return**

You can submit your VAT return using HMRC’s online services or through MTD-compatible software. Once you have submitted your return, you will receive an acknowledgement from HMRC confirming that it has been received. You should retain this acknowledgement for your records.

If you cannot submit your return by the deadline, you should contact HMRC as soon as possible. In some circumstances, we may be able to agree a different date for submission, but you must request this before the deadline has passed. A request made after the deadline will not be treated as a valid application for an extension.

**Payment of VAT due**

Any VAT due for the quarter must be paid to HMRC by the same date as the return is due. Payment can be made by direct debit, bank transfer, or through your MTD-compatible software. If you pay by direct debit, you must ensure that your bank account has sufficient funds on the payment date. HMRC may charge interest on any VAT paid late, and you may also be liable to a surcharge if you do not pay on time.

If you are due a repayment, HMRC will normally make the payment within 10 working days of receiving your return, provided the return is accurate and complete. If you are due a repayment and you also owe VAT for a previous period, HMRC may offset the repayment against the amount you owe.

**Late submission of VAT returns**

Submitting VAT returns late is a serious matter. HMRC may charge a default surcharge if you do not submit a return by the due date. The surcharge is calculated as a percentage of the VAT that is unpaid at the date the surcharge is triggered. The percentage increases with each successive default within a 12-month period.

For the first default, the surcharge is 2% of the VAT outstanding. For a second default within the same period, the surcharge rises to 5%. For a third default, it rises to 10%, and for a fourth or subsequent default, it rises to 15%. In addition to the surcharge, you may also be liable to interest on any VAT that is paid late.

documents.content:
You are responsible for monitoring your taxable turnover on a rolling 12-month basis. This is not the same as your accounting year. You must look back at the total value of your taxable supplies made in the last 12 months at the end of every month. If, at the end of any month, the total for the previous 12 months has exceeded the threshold, you must register within 30 days.

The date of registration will be the date you became liable to register, which is the end of the month in which the threshold was exceeded. You will then be required to charge VAT on your supplies from that date, even if you have not yet received your VAT registration number.

**3. What Counts as Taxable Turnover**

For the purposes of the threshold, taxable turnover includes the total value of all supplies you make in the course or furtherance of your business that are subject to VAT at the standard, reduced, or zero rate. It also includes supplies that would be taxable if they were made in the United Kingdom.

The following are not included in your taxable turnover:

- Supplies that are exempt from VAT, such as certain financial services, education, and health services.
- Supplies made outside the UK that would not be taxable if made in the UK.
- Capital assets sold as part of a business transfer.
- Grants or subsidies that are not directly linked to the value of supplies.

If you make only exempt supplies, you will not normally be able to register for VAT. However, there are limited circumstances where you may be able to register voluntarily, for example, if you make certain types of exempt supplies to customers outside the UK.

**4. Voluntary Registration**

If your taxable turnover is below the threshold, you may still choose to register for VAT voluntarily. This can be beneficial if you make mostly zero-rated supplies and expect to reclaim VAT on your purchases, or if you wish to recover input tax on costs incurred before you become liable to register.

You should note that once you are registered voluntarily, you must remain registered for at least 12 months. If you wish to cancel your registration at the end of that period, you may do so provided your taxable turnover in the following 12 months is expected to be below the deregistration threshold.

**5. Deregistration Threshold**

The deregistration threshold is also reviewed annually. If you are registered for VAT and your taxable turnover in the next 12 months is expected to fall below the deregistration threshold, you may apply to cancel your registration. You should contact HMRC if you think you may be eligible to deregister.

**6. Effect of the Threshold on Group Registrations**

If you are part of a group of companies that is registered for VAT as a single entity, the threshold applies to the total taxable turnover of the group, not to each individual company. You should therefore monitor the combined turnover of all group members. If the group’s total taxable turnover exceeds the threshold, the group must register.

**7. Changes to the Threshold During the Year**

The threshold is set for the tax year beginning 1 April and ending 31 March the following year. Any changes to the threshold are announced in the Budget and take effect from the start of the next tax year. You should not assume that the threshold will remain the same from year to year.

**8. Penalties for Late Registration**

If you fail to register by the required date, HMRC may charge a penalty. The penalty is calculated as a percentage of the VAT that is due from the date you should have registered to the date you actually registered. The percentage is based on the reason for the failure, and whether it was deliberate or non-deliberate.

If you become aware that you should have registered earlier, you should contact HMRC as soon as possible. In some cases, we may reduce the penalty if you have a reasonable excuse for the late registration.

This certificate confirms that the person named above is registered for Value Added Tax with effect from the date shown. The registration has been granted under the provisions of the Value Added Tax Act 1994 and is subject to the conditions and obligations set out in the VAT guide (Notice 700) and any other relevant notices.

Please keep this certificate in a safe place. You may be asked to show it as proof of your VAT registration status. If you lose this certificate, you can request a replacement through your HMRC online services account or by contacting the VAT helpline.

Your VAT registration number must appear on all VAT invoices, credit notes, and any other documents that you are required to issue. It should also be shown on your business stationery and on any website that you use for business purposes.

Registration details held by HMRC

The details shown above are based on the information you provided in your application. You must tell HMRC about any changes to these details within 30 days of the change. This includes changes to your business name, address, contact details, or the nature of your business activities.

If you change your business address, you can update your details online. You will need your VAT registration number and your Government Gateway user ID to do this. If you do not have online access, you can write to the address shown at the end of this notice.

Your obligations as a registered person

As a registered person, you are required to:

- Charge VAT at the correct rate on all taxable supplies you make.
- Keep sufficient records to support the VAT returns you submit.
- Submit VAT returns to HMRC by the due date, even if there is no VAT to pay or reclaim.
- Pay any VAT due to HMRC by the due date.
- Issue valid VAT invoices to your customers for all taxable supplies.
- Display this certificate if you are required to do so at your business premises.

Failure to meet these obligations may result in penalties or interest charges. If you are unsure about any of your obligations, you should refer to Notice 700 or contact the VAT helpline.

VAT return periods

Your VAT return period will normally be every three months. Your first return period will begin on the date your registration becomes effective. HMRC will send you a notice telling you the dates of your return periods and the deadlines for submitting returns and paying any VAT due.

For most businesses, the deadline for submitting a VAT return and paying any VAT due is one calendar month and seven days after the end of the return period. For example, if your return period ends on 31 March, the deadline is 7 May.

You can choose to submit your VAT returns monthly if you wish. This may help you manage your cash flow if you regularly reclaim more VAT than you charge. You can also choose to use the Annual Accounting Scheme if your taxable turnover is below the threshold for that scheme. Details of all available schemes are in Notice 700.

VAT invoices

When you make a taxable supply to another business, you must issue a full VAT invoice. A full VAT invoice must show:

- an invoice number that is unique and sequential
- the date of issue
- your name and address
- your VAT registration number
- the name and address of the customer
- a description of the goods or services supplied
- the quantity of goods or the extent of services supplied
- the rate of VAT charged and the amount of VAT, expressed in sterling
- the total amount payable, excluding VAT, and the total amount payable including VAT

documents.title: HMRC VAT Registration Notice
documents.content:
HMRC VAT Registration Notice

Issued: 15 April 2025

Reference: VAT 405

This notice provides general guidance for businesses that have recently registered for VAT or are considering registration. It should be read alongside Notice 700, which contains more detailed information about how VAT works.

Record keeping

You must keep records of all business transactions that affect your VAT position. These records should be accurate, complete, and readable. You must keep them for at least six years, unless you have written permission from HMRC to destroy them earlier. Records may be kept on paper or in electronic form, provided they are readily accessible to HMRC when required.

Your records should include:

- your accounting records, including cash books, sales and purchase ledgers, and bank statements
- your VAT account, which summarises the VAT you have charged and the VAT you have paid
- copies of VAT invoices you have issued and VAT invoices you have received
- documentation relating to imports and exports
- any credit notes or debit notes you have issued or received
- records of goods and services you have supplied to yourself or to your staff for private use

Your VAT account must show, for each VAT return period, the total VAT due on your sales, the total VAT you can reclaim on your purchases, and the net amount payable to HMRC or reclaimable from HMRC. You should update your VAT account regularly and make sure it agrees with your accounting records.

Electronic records

If you keep your records electronically, you must ensure that the software you use can produce, in a legible format, all the information that HMRC may need to verify your VAT position. You must also ensure that the records cannot be altered without leaving an audit trail. You should take reasonable steps to protect your records from loss or corruption, including keeping backup copies.

Digital record keeping is a mandatory requirement for most businesses under the Making Tax Digital for VAT rules. If you are required to keep digital records, you must use functional compatible software to maintain your VAT account and file your returns. Further information is available in Notice 700/22.

Invoicing

You must issue a VAT invoice whenever you make a taxable supply to another business. You do not have to issue a VAT invoice for sales to private individuals, but you must be able to account for the VAT on those sales. You may issue a less detailed invoice for retail sales where the total amount including VAT is £250 or less. A less detailed invoice must show your name and address, your VAT registration number, the date of issue, a description of the goods or services, and the total amount payable including VAT.

If you issue a VAT invoice, you must keep a copy. You must not issue a VAT invoice for a supply that is exempt from VAT or that is outside the scope of VAT, unless the invoice clearly states that no VAT is chargeable.

Credit notes

If you allow a customer a reduction in the price after you have issued a VAT invoice, you must issue a credit note. The credit note must show the same information as the original invoice, together with the amount of the reduction and the VAT adjustment. You must keep a copy of every credit note you issue and you should ensure that your accounting records reflect the adjustment.

Filing your returns

You must submit a VAT return for each return period, even if you have no VAT to pay or reclaim. The return must be submitted electronically using compatible software. You should allow sufficient time to prepare your return and to submit it before the deadline. HMRC will not accept returns submitted by post unless you have received specific permission to do so.
